title: Ni mucho menos: reforzar una negación

sections.content: Ni mucho menos (let alone, much less) reinforces a negation by ruling out an even stronger or more extreme possibility -- useful for emphasizing just how far something falls short. It typically follows the thing already denied, adding a second, more emphatic denial. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Varios cientos de lenguas propias, ninguna de ellas, ni mucho menos, reducible a una sola cultura homogénea.
items.english: Several hundred distinct languages, none of them reducible, let alone, to a single homogeneous culture.

items.spanish: La mayoría de los Estados ni siquiera reconocían esta diversidad, y ni mucho menos concedían derechos diferenciados.
items.english: Most states didn't even recognize this diversity, much less grant differentiated rights.

items.spanish: El gobierno no consultó a las comunidades, y ni mucho menos buscó su consentimiento antes de actuar.
items.english: The government didn't consult the communities, let alone seek their consent before acting.

items.spanish: Nadie esperaba una victoria fácil, y ni mucho menos un cambio tan profundo en tan poco tiempo.
items.english: No one expected an easy victory, much less such a profound change in so little time.

sections.content: Ni mucho menos almost always pairs with a first negation (ni siquiera, no, nadie) that it then intensifies -- it rarely opens a sentence on its own, since it needs something weaker to escalate from.
